transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-01-04
- Time: 15:00 - 15:47 UTC
- Duration: 47 minutes
- Attendees: Sofia Ramirez (Redwood AE), Daniel Cho (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Marlin procurement), Ben Ortiz (Marlin Infosec), Clara Voss (Marlin Legal), Evan Liu (Marlin Cloud)

Summary:
Quick intake to validate final commercial pathway (hosted vs dedicated vs private), discuss MSA/DPA exceptions, privileged keying/KMS flow, and timing for pricing approval. Agreement to run a short benchmark and circulate redlines/pricing matrix.

Topics covered:
- MSA and DPA redline expectations and exceptions
- SLA tiers and rollback/fallback policies for sensitive workflows
- KMS/HSM and customer key management options (privileged keying)
- Pricing thresholds and procurement approval path
- Short benchmark to validate latency/cost tradeoffs

References shared during call:
- onboarding packet: https://rwd.co/onboard-marlin (deck)
- quick benchmark sheet: https://rwd.co/bench-marlin
- security summary pdf: https://rwd.co/sec-marlin-pkg

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Ramirez: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Aisha Khan: Aisha here.
[00:08] Ben Ortiz: Ben on infosec.
[00:10] Clara Voss: Clara from legal.
[00:12] Evan Liu: Evan, cloud eng.
[00:14] Daniel Cho: Daniel, SE at Redwood.
[00:16] Sofia Ramirez: Great, our agenda is short; want to confirm path to commercial signoff, any DPA/MSA exceptions, and scope a quick benchmark.

[02:03] Aisha Khan: From procurement perspective we have two gating items: pricing band and any data residency obligations. Marlin has EU customer data we need to keep in region for a subset. Does Redwood support region-only hosting for that dataset?
[02:22] Daniel Cho: Yes, we have regional routing - hosted regions and Dedicated placement. For privacy we can do a Private deployment if needed, or Dedicated capacity pinned to eu-west, that meets residency. There is a tiny nuance around audit logs — if you need customer-managed logging, we support pushing audit logs to your syslog/Splunk via our VPC connector, though that typically feeds into the Private plus control plane flow.
[02:47] Ben Ortiz: Auditing is critical, also SOC 2 type 2 and ISO 27001 proofs. Can we get the artifacts?
[02:55] Sofia Ramirez: Absolutely, we shared a security packet in the calendar invite and I just posted the link in chat. The packet includes SOC 2 attestation, encryption at rest, and our standard DPA. We can also run an on-site or virtual security review if needed.

[04:30] Clara Voss: Looking at the DPA, we have a handful of asks: liability cap, deletion timelines, and the privileged keying clause. We prefer customer-managed keys if possible for certain regulated workflows.
[04:45] Daniel Cho: For privileged keying we do have two models—Redwood-managed KMS where keys are in our KMS but tenant-scoped, or customer-managed keys via your KMS/HSM and an envelope encryption approach. There is an operational difference: customer keys require extra onboarding and a short privileged access playbook. Also, note a small latency delta in some edge cases when key unwrap is done.
[05:20] Evan Liu: That sounds fine. We need to know the exact onboarding steps and if there's any privileged access escalation for emergency key rotation.
[05:31] Sofia Ramirez: We'll include that in the redlined MSA notes. Clara, any hard stops on liability cap?
[05:40] Clara Voss: Standard exceptions—we're asking for carve-outs for third-party breaches and a clearer SLA crediting method, not just vague language. Also want a 30-day data deletion guarantee for deleted customer records.

[07:00] Daniel Cho: SLA-wise we have tiered SLOs for hosted: 99.5% uptime for standard, and 99.9% for dedicated with an option for higher with reserved capacity. Credits are applied per incident based on latency/availability thresholds. We can share the exact SLA formula in the appendix.
[07:24] Ben Ortiz: How do rollbacks and fallbacks work? If a model variant fails do you fallback to a smaller model automatically? That has implications for accuracy and for our compliance if PII is being processed.
[07:39] Daniel Cho: Yes, we have automated routing policies—fallback to a compatible model variant or route to a Dedicated reserve. Important note: any fallback model may have different tokenization/behavior so for sensitive PII pipelines we recommend pinning model version and enabling strict fail-open or fail-closed behavior. We'll document options.

[09:10] Aisha Khan: On pricing, procurement needs a clear band for three months after pilot. We need to know committed spend levels for a discount ladder and what triggers pricing committee review.
[09:26] Sofia Ramirez: Typically we provide pilot pricing for 30 days, then a pricing ladder if they commit to reserved capacity. For Dedicated we can lock in a monthly commit with a discount — the tiers are 0-5k GPU hours, 5-20k, and 20k+. I'll share a more explicit pricing matrix after this call.
[09:52] Evan Liu: For the pilot we'd like a predictable budget envelope. Can we cap token throughput or set rate limits to control cost?
[10:03] Daniel Cho: Yes, rate limiting and per-route quotas are configurable at the token level and route level. You can also set cost alerts and token caps per API key. We'll show screenshots of console controls in the packet.

[12:15] Clara Voss: Back to DPA—what about subprocessors? We need the list and a 30-day notice for any new subprocessor.
[12:25] Sofia Ramirez: We include that by default; our DPA has a subprocessors list and we provide notices before changes. For gov/regulated customers we can negotiate stricter controls.

[14:00] Ben Ortiz: A technical question—how is KV cache handled? Our concern is leak of cache between tenants.
[14:10] Daniel Cho: KV cache is segregated per tenant; we use memory isolation and per-request namespaces. There have been occasional transcription artifacts where people say K V cache as separate words but it's the same construct. For Dedicated we can even pin cache eviction policies.

[16:20] Aisha Khan: Procurement also flagged escrow and continuity: if Redwood is acquired or stops servicing certain models, what is the exit path? Data export timelines and portability?
[16:35] Sofia Ramirez: Exit clauses: standard export tooling, data export in JSON/NDJSON formats, and we can propose an escrow-style cadence for long-term contracts where source keys for model artifacts and data extracts are periodically deposited with an escrow provider. We'll add language to the MSA about 60-day export windows on termination.

[18:45] Clara Voss: One more legal nuance—are we able to get a limited warranty for accuracy or at least a rollback credit if model behavior regresses post-deploy?
[18:58] Daniel Cho: We can't warranty model outputs for correctness, but for service regressions we have quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to evals; for severe regressions we can do service credits or rollback policies as defined in the SLA appendix. We will outline the detection and remediation playbook.

[22:10] Aisha Khan: Okay, timeline wise procurement needs the redlined MSA and a pricing readout to start the internal approver chain by next Monday. Can Redwood commit to that?
[22:22] Sofia Ramirez: Yes, I can share a redline by Friday EOD 1/8. Daniel will run the bench and share results the following week.

[25:00] Daniel Cho: Quick note on the benchmark—we suggest using a representative sample of 50k tokens across shortest and longest queries and testing in three modes: hosted (eu-west region), Dedicated small pool, and Dedicated with caching on. We'll capture p95 latency, throughput, and effective cost per 1k tokens.
[25:28] Evan Liu: We'll provide the sample queries and a CSV of traffic profile by tomorrow.

[28:00] Ben Ortiz: On privileged keying, what's the emergency rotation process? If customer keys are rotated outside Redwood, do you support rewrap without downtime?
[28:12] Daniel Cho: We have a key rotation protocol; customer key rotatation requires a brief reconciliation window but is designed to be non-disruptive. In practice there's a small spike in token latency while we re-derive keys, typically a few hundred milliseconds per cold call. We'll document SLA impact.

[31:00] Clara Voss: Another ask—can we add a clause for audit rights and periodic pen test reports?
[31:12] Sofia Ramirez: Yes, we provide yearly penetration test summaries and can negotiate more frequent scans for enterprise engagements. We also offer on-site or remote SOC review under an NDA.

[33:40] Aisha Khan: For the procurement approval matrix—who in Redwood signs pricing off? I need a contact for the pricing committee if I need an exception.
[33:52] Sofia Ramirez: I'm your AE rep and the escalation is to our commercial ops team; I'll include the contact in the next email. Pricing exceptions typically go to commercial_ops@redwood.com and require a one-pager justification.

[36:20] Evan Liu: Operational question—what's the onboarding ETA for Dedicated if we sign by Feb? We have a launch window late March.
[36:32] Daniel Cho: For Dedicated, typical provisioning is 4-6 weeks from order due to GPU scheduling and network setup. If you need faster we can prioritize with a committed upfront deposit and expedite with partners. Private deployment or VPC deployments may add more time depending on infra.

[38:10] Sofia Ramirez: Recap: action items are redline MSA/DPA by Sofia, bench by Daniel, Marlin to send sample queries and procurement matrix. We agreed pilot pricing for 30 days and a likely move to Dedicated if the bench shows cost/latency wins.

[40:00] Aisha Khan: Quick objection—pricing: we're sensitive to egress fees. If Dedicated is in our VPC, are there still egress charges?
[40:12] Daniel Cho: Egress depends on routing. For Private/VPC we can often avoid public egress fees. Dedicated in our cloud will still have provider egress charges; we can model that in the bench. We'll include an explicit egress line item in the pricing sheet.

[43:00] Ben Ortiz: Last sec: competitor callouts—we've looked at Anthropic and some self-hosted runtimes. What's Redwood's differentiator for us?
[43:14] Sofia Ramirez: We're focused on production-grade inference with tooling to control cost: intelligent batching, prefix/KV caching, and rollout controls. Also unified ops across hosted, dedicated, and private — meaning one set of APIs and rollouts independent of infra. We'll send a short one-pager.

[45:30] Clara Voss: Sounds good. If you can get the MSA/DPA redline and the pricing ladder in the next week we'll run procurement's intake.
[45:42] Sofia Ramirez: Note taken. We'll share the artifacts and set up a follow-up next week to review the bench.

[46:20] Sofia Ramirez: Okay thank you everyone. We'll follow up in email and upload docs to the shared drive.
[46:28] Aisha Khan: Thanks.
[46:30] Ben Ortiz: Thanks all.
[46:32] Clara Voss: Bye.

Call end.

Post-call quick notes (auto-gen, may contain errors):
- transcription had a few mis-heard acronyms (KMS vs K M S) and product names, check links in notes.
- procurement asked for a pricing cap and explicit egress line item.
- next meeting tentatively scheduled for 2026-01-13 to review bench results and redline feedback.
